A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same USplat4D work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments, DyCheck tracking results, ablations, and runtime measurements in the main paper and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds HyperNeRF results, parameter studies, runtime scaling measurements, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 adds a downstream motion-segmentation procedure: cluster the key-graph weights and assign non-key Gaussians to those groups through their connections (Figure 7). The underlying uncertainty estimation, graph construction, and reconstruction pipeline remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual HyperNeRF evaluation in Appendix C.7/Figure S2, whereas v1 only cites or discusses that dataset. Figure 7 also demonstrates multi-object motion segmentation. The existing DyCheck, DAVIS, Objaverse, and NVIDIA coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The comparison methods are retained. 4DGS already participates in v1's seven-scene DyCheck evaluation; v2 supplies its missing per-scene entries in Table S3 and reuses it for HyperNeRF. These additions do not establish a new comparator set for the retained experiments.

E3.justification: New experiments sweep color thresholds, significant-period thresholds, and depth scaling, and vary Objaverse sequence length for runtime evaluation. Existing benchmark resolutions, camera trajectories, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; the equal-time comparison was already present in v1.

E4.justification: v2 adds three parameter-sensitivity studies (Tables S7–S9), runtime-versus-length analysis (Figure S3), graph-grouping analysis (Figure 7), and concrete textureless, fast-motion, and deforming-object case studies (Figures S4–S6). The spatial-sampling ablation is retained from v1 Table S7 and moved into Table 3(d), rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting. Per-Gaussian uncertainty is a model component, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Principal benchmark, tracking, NVIDIA, and equal-time results are retained. Substantial new results include HyperNeRF detail-region scores, parameter sweeps, runtime curves, motion grouping, and challenging-case findings. For example, Figure S2 newly reports PSNR 26.59 for 4DGS versus 28.34 for USplat4D on one highlighted region. Table S3 also fills missing 4DGS scene-level results.

T1.justification: Equation 11 changes both non-key-loss summations from all nodes V to non-key nodes Vn, correcting the formal domain to match the surrounding description. The uncertainty derivation in Appendix A.1 is retained, and no new proof is introduced. This does not establish that the training implementation changed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: model-agnostic, time-varying Gaussian uncertainty guides graph-based optimization to improve motion consistency and extreme-view reconstruction. The added analyses support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v1's brief prior-failure discussion becomes detailed analysis of textureless tracking, scaffold constraints, fast and non-rigid motion, rolling-shutter artifacts, and sparse observations in v2 Appendix E. New explanations address parameter sensitivity and motion grouping. Section 5.2 also strengthens 'nearly all' to 'all metrics,' despite an unchanged Table 1 exception.

D1.justification: v2 newly states the color threshold as 0.50 and axis scaling as [1, 1, 0.01] in Appendix D. Existing training schedules, hardware, loss weights, data curation, and project URL remain. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed main-experiment settings; Table S9's reference labeling remains inconsistent.

R1.justification: v2 adds Engel et al. (2017) on Direct Sparse Odometry and Von Luxburg (2007) on spectral clustering, and develops more specific comparisons with SoM/MoSca constraints. The main related-work positioning is retained. Publication updates to existing references do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most original exposition remains. v2 makes local wording corrections, renames Section 5.1, rewrites the conclusion, removes the appendix outline, moves the sampling-ablation discussion into the main text, and organizes challenging cases into Appendix E, moving broader impacts to F.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 7 and Figures S2–S6, covering segmentation, HyperNeRF, runtime scaling, and challenging cases, plus three sensitivity tables. It merges v1 Table S7 into Table 3(d), extends Table S3, revises several figure arrangements, and relocates retained tables and figures.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's generic failure discussion and unspecified settings, v2 provides useful parameter disclosures, sensitivity evidence, and concrete failure analyses, improving reproducibility and assessment of robustness. The gains are limited by reporting problems: Table S9 has inconsistent reference labeling, and the strengthened 'all metrics' claim overlooks MoBlender's better LPIPS in unchanged Table 1. Overall, the additions provide a modest net quality improvement.
